title: Lotus-seed dormancy: ultra-wide-bandgap gain cell that holds charge for years
idea: Sacred lotus seeds stay viable for ~1,300 years by sealing a dormant embryo in an impermeable coat. Build a 2T gain cell whose access transistor has an ultra-wide-bandgap channel (Ga2O3 or AlGaN, Eg 4.8-6 eV) and a ferroelectric back gate that stays polarized to deep depletion when power drops. Storage-node leakage falls below ~10^-24 A, so a 1 fF node keeps its level for years.
why: Makes a DRAM-structure cell non-volatile with no exotic storage physics: DRAM-like write and read speed, unlimited endurance (charge on a node, no wear) and no refresh. BEOL-compatible.

title: Multilayer optical-disc focus addressing via threshold-coded tiers
idea: Like BD-XL picking a layer by focus depth, give each of 32 storage tiers on one shared vertical wordline a distinct access threshold set by deposited channel thickness; address tier k by stepping wordline voltage and differencing successive bitline reads, and write each column in descending-threshold order.
why: 10x at same cost: removes per-tier bitline staircases and select lines, so 32 tiers cost about one hole etch plus depositions; ~15x bits per footprint.

title: Martian colonist: biased antiferroelectric ZrO2 bit in one vacuum tool
idea: A Mars colonist has no water, only vacuum. Asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes give an antiferroelectric ZrO2 film a built-in bias, so one of its two field-induced polar states persists at zero volts. The whole electrode-dielectric-electrode stack is deposited in one cluster tool without breaking vacuum, with in-situ atomic-hydrogen cleans in place of wet RCA cleans.
why: A quasi-non-volatile AFE cell (fact 3) with AFE endurance above 1e12. Avoiding air breaks removes ~8 wet clean and rinse steps from the cell module and cuts its UPW use by more than 10x.

title: Apollo core rope: toroidal nanomagnet rings with coincident-current selection
idea: Stimulus 'Apollo core memory' -> revive ferrite-core memory at 100 nm: each bit is a closed-flux CoFeB nanoring whose clockwise/counterclockwise circulation flips only where two half-select currents in a crossbar coincide, so no access transistor is needed. Read uses a tunnel junction on one arc of the ring.
why: Removes the access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3), turns the array into a pure BEOL crossbar stackable in tiers (fact 2), and flux closure gives zero stray field for tight packing.

title: National capacitor-module line where startups drop in new storage elements
idea: Box as infrastructure: a government-anchored 300 mm U.S. line runs standard domestic periphery and access-transistor wafers to the capacitor level, then lets startups insert their own storage-element module (AAO, CNT, rutile TiO2, AlBN and others) and finishes BEOL. Teams pay per wafer and keep their IP.
why: Capital intensity (Fact 4): proving a new storage element costs ~$50M instead of a $15B fab and shortens lab-to-1-Gb proof from ~8 years to ~3.

title: Retool idle U.S. thin-film PV and flexible-display lines as memory fabs
idea: IFR: memory capacity appears without building fabs. Closest achievable: buy or lease idle R2R thin-film PV and flexible OLED lines, add a printed storage-element module, and ship foil memory tiers within 12-18 months.
why: Capital and time (fact 4): line cost ~$100M vs $15B; raises U.S. manufacturability.

title: Vacuum as the insulator: field-emission two-terminal crossbar storage cell
idea: Reverse insulator and conductor: each storage node is a metal island over a sealed 3-5 nm vacuum gap to a sharp emitter at a wordline/bitline crossing; below the Fowler-Nordheim threshold the gap passes essentially nothing, while ~2x the field drives uA emission to charge or discharge it in ns.
why: Leakage tail and 3D blocker (facts 2,3): super-exponential I-V gives >1e12 on/off with no transistor, so 4F2 crossbar tiers can stack with no lateral transistor at all.

title: Gold-leaf electroscope: suspended graphene leaf holds charge in vacuum
idea: Store the bit as charge on a suspended graphene (or 20-nm SiN/Al) leaf in a sealed cavity, touching nothing but its clamp on thick thermal oxide; electrostatic repulsion deflects it a few nm, sensed capacitively by an underlying electrode without discharge, and charge is written or erased by field emission across a 5-nm vacuum gap to a sharp tip.
why: Facts 3 and 8: no junction or thin dielectric sits in the leakage path, so retention is set by negligible low-field emission, and read is non-destructive (no restore energy); built with graphene transfer, e-beam and critical-point drying; ns sensing of nm deflection is the risk.

title: Jazz drummer's frozen groove: hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2
idea: A jazz drummer can hold a groove after the band stops. In 1T-TaS2 a single ~30 ps electrical pulse switches the electrons' charge-density-wave pattern into a hidden metallic order that persists, and a second, longer pulse restores the insulating order; the bit reads as a ~10x resistance change.
why: ps switching at fJ energy and non-volatile storage (facts 3, 10).

title: Po: memory made of molasses — thermally selected glassy-electrolyte crossbar
idea: Po: memory made of molasses. Extracted: print a crossbar of polymer electrolyte that is glassy (ions frozen) at operating temperature but softens above Tg; a coincident current pulse heats only the selected crossing above Tg so ions drift to set its conductance, then it re-freezes, making heat the selector.
why: Transistorless, solution-printed stacked layers aim at a 100x cost cut. Trade-offs: us thermal writes, thermal crosstalk, lower endurance.

title: Racetrack without current: VCMA peristaltic domain-wall pumping
idea: IBM's racetrack stalled because moving domain walls needed ~1e7-1e8 A/cm2 and walls pinned randomly. Lay three-phase gate electrodes along a short 16-bit CoFeB/MgO track: sequential voltage-controlled anisotropy waves, a local electrostatic version of bubble memory's rotating field, push every wall one notch per clock with no current through the track.
why: Shift energy drops from pJ to ~fJ per bit (CV2 only); 16 bits per access transistor gives ~2F2/bit and shrinks periphery per bit (Fact 7).

title: Matryoshka coaxial multi-shell capacitor by sequential annular ALD casting
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: inside each pillar footprint grow three concentric electrode shells separated by dielectric, alternately strapped to storage node and plate (interdigitated coax), by repeating ALD electrode/dielectric/sacrificial-carbon fill and recess-etch cycles. Contradiction resolved: more electrode area vs. same footprint and lower aspect ratio.
why: Fact 1: ~2.5-3x Cs per footprint, or equal Cs at AR ~30:1 instead of 60-75:1, easing etch, bending and collapse.

title: Nested triple-coaxial cylinder capacitor like an MLCC in a pillar
idea: IFR: every bit of cell volume is capacitor plate. Closest achievable: build three concentric electrodes inside one pillar hole by alternating ALD electrode, dielectric and sacrificial layers, tying alternate shells together at top and bottom as an MLCC interdigitates its plates.
why: Fact 1: ~2.5-3x Cs per pillar vs a single cylinder, so AR can fall from ~70 to ~30.

title: Blacksmith's temper: martensite variant bit in NiTi nanopillars
idea: A blacksmith keeps memory in the crystal structure of steel. In a NiTi or Cu-Al-Ni nanopillar, a short voltage and heat pulse selects one of two martensite twin variants (ferroelastic switching); the variant is read through piezoresistance or the strain-coupled threshold shift of an attached transistor.
why: A non-volatile structural bit that holds no charge, so nothing leaks (fact 3), built from earth-abundant metals.

title: NRAM with exactly one nanotube junction per cell via DNA origami
idea: Nantero NRAM stalled on random CNT fabrics: a variable number of tube junctions per cell spread the switching distribution, and the feedstock needed costly purification. Use DNA-origami templates anchored in lithographic binding sites to place exactly two crossed CNTs per cell (chirality purity is irrelevant because switching is electromechanical), then strip the DNA with an O2 plasma.
why: Narrow switching distributions at ~20 nm cells; nonvolatile vdW latch with no refresh; the bit element is placed by self-assembly rather than EUV.

title: Anodized-aluminum nanopore templates as litho-free capacitor holes
idea: Borrow the electrolytic-capacitor industry's anodization: deposit Al over the access-transistor array, anodize it into self-ordered hexagonal nanopores (AR >200, pitch set by anodizing voltage), and line each pore with ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN as the storage capacitor. A shallow dimple pre-pattern on the landing pads registers each pore to its transistor.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and EUV/capital (fact 4): AR 115-200 comes from a wet electrochemical bath instead of HAR plasma etch plus a hard-mask EUV layer; ~1.5-2x Cs or ~30% capacitor-module cost cut.

title: Po: nobody knows where the bits are — random nanoparticle self-mapped crossbar
idea: Po: nobody knows where the bits are. Extracted: spin-coat charge-storing nanoparticles at random between two imprinted line grids; after fabrication the chip probes every crossing, keeps those with a working node, and stores the map in a small on-die table, replacing costly placement with a one-time self-test.
why: Takes alignment, CD control and yield out of cost (fact 4), so $1/m2-class coating plus self-mapping aims at 100x. Trade-offs: 30-60% unused crossings and map overhead.

title: Ni: Ni(OH)2 pseudocapacitive storage node stores tens of times more charge
idea: Coat the storage electrode with 2-3 nm of Ni(OH)2 and a thin solid proton conductor so a write drives faradaic Ni2+/Ni3+ redox, whose pseudocapacitance (hundreds of uF/cm2) is tens of times a high-k dielectric (~7 uF/cm2); the charge dumps onto the bit line like a normal DRAM read.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1): a planar or low-AR node holds 5+ fF; nickel is widely available; redox rate at ~10 ns and electrolyte leakage are the risks.

title: Bank-wide floating-body refresh fired in a single REF slot
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): REF commands keep arriving on the spec schedule. Use bistable floating-body cells whose parasitic bipolar transistor latches, so one REF fires a bank-wide source pulse that pumps '1' cells back to full hole charge by impact ionization while '0' cells stay empty, restoring every row at once; the remaining REFs become no-ops.
why: Cuts refresh energy (46 fJ/bit, fact 3) and refresh activations (fact 9) ~1000x via parallel restore in a capacitorless 4F2 cell; bipolar latch margin across temperature is the risk.

title: Ice cube tray: nanopore fills or drains, 80x capacitance swing
idea: Stimulus 'ice cube tray' (each cell full or empty) -> each cell is a 10 nm hydrophobic nanopore connected to a sealed water reservoir; such pores are bistable (liquid-filled vs vapor-filled), and an electrowetting pulse fills one while a reverse pulse triggers capillary drying. Water (k~80) vs vapor (k~1) changes pore capacitance ~80x, a giant read signal.
why: Huge per-cell signal removes the 5 fF capacitor requirement (fact 1); the state is thermodynamic, not leaking charge, so no refresh (fact 3); planar cell with no deep etch (fact 4).

title: Plated-wire memory rebuilt as vertical plated vias in 3D stacks
idea: Plated-wire memory (Voyager era) stored bits in the circumferential magnetization of permalloy plated on a wire and read them non-destructively by tilting it with a word strap. Make the wire a vertical copper pillar in a 3D-NAND-style hole lined with circumferentially anisotropic CoFeB, use the stacked tier planes as word straps, write by coincident pillar plus strap current, and read by a small strap pulse that tilts the film and induces a pillar voltage.
why: 100+ tiers from one hole etch with no lateral transistor or capacitor (Fact 2), non-destructive read (Fact 8), non-volatile (Fact 3); ~1/5 the cost per bit of 2D DRAM if signal suffices.

title: Silicon-carbide CMOS foundry DRAM for 200 C environments
idea: MAGNIFY bandgap from 1.1 to 3.3 eV using a commercial 4H-SiC CMOS MPW: 1T1C or gain cells whose intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm^-3 (vs 1e10 in Si) retain data at 200 C longer than silicon DRAM does at 25 C; a small team sells into down-hole, aerospace and EV-inverter markets.
why: Refresh-light memory at extreme temperatures (fact 3), U.S. SiC fabs, no EUV; pulls niche demand off silicon DRAM.

title: Champagne fizz: electrolytic nanobubble toggles nanochannel resistance
idea: Stimulus 'champagne bubble' -> a 15 nm nanochannel holds dilute aqueous electrolyte between two carbon electrodes; a short pulse electrolyzes a few thousand molecules into an insulating H2 nanobubble that pins in a hydrophobic pocket (bit 1), and a reverse pulse recombines and dissolves it (bit 0). Read is a 0.1 V resistance probe with >100x contrast.
why: A bit with no stored charge and no filament defects (unlike ReRAM): attacks refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor wall (fact 1); huge on/off ratio allows ~4F^2 cells.

title: Softgel nanocapsule: sealed ionic-liquid double-layer capacitor per cell
idea: Use pharmaceutical softgel encapsulation: fill each cup with an imidazolium ionic liquid (C, H, N, O, S, F) and seal it under an ALD Al2O3 lid. Charge sits in the ~1 nm electric double layer at carbon or TiN electrodes, at ~15-20 uF/cm2 (10-20x an oxide dielectric) and ~ns RC at 10 nm scale.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF from an AR ~8 cup. Inside the electrochemical window there is no dielectric tunneling leakage, and the materials are commodity organics.

title: Hand warmer: undercooled liquid tin nanodot versus solid tin
idea: Stimulus 'click-disc hand warmer' (supercooled liquid that crystallizes on a click) -> tin nanodots embedded in SiO2 (formed by thermal dewetting, no etch) can stay liquid ~150 K below their 232 C melting point; a Joule pulse melts a dot (1) and a sharp field or acoustic 'click' nucleates crystallization (0). Liquid tin is ~3x more resistive than solid, read nondestructively.
why: A new phase-memory class with no amorphous drift and tiny nanoscale latent heat, nonvolatile within the undercooling window (fact 3); fluorine-free dewetting fabrication.

title: Swap inert TiN electrode for pseudocapacitive MXene intercalation electrode
idea: Coat the storage node with a Ti3C2 MXene film against a thin solid proton conductor. Proton intercalation between MXene layers adds Faradaic pseudocapacitance (hundreds of uF/cm2 in bulk) to the double layer, and MXenes are among the fastest-rate pseudocapacitive materials known.
why: Over 10x areal capacitance (fact 1) from abundant Ti and C, unlike RuO2, which needs scarce Ru; a planar or shallow cap at DUV pitch can store DRAM-level charge.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Replace the high-k dielectric with a 2-3 nm fast proton conductor (hydrated Ta2O5 or CsH2PO4-like film) between ion-blocking electrodes, so stored charge sits in Helmholtz double layers ~0.3 nm from each electrode, an effective k >200.
why: Fact 1: 10-20 uF/cm2 areal capacitance (vs ~4-6 for ZrO2 stacks) puts 5 fF in a planar or AR<15 node; the open question is whether sub-nm ion relaxation charges in ns at 2 nm.

title: Eliminate dielectric thickness limits: solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor storage node
idea: Eliminate the conventional capacitor dielectric: the storage node is a nano-electrode against a thin solid ion conductor (protonic phosphosilicate or LiPON) with blocking electrodes, so the sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~20-40 uF/cm2) supplies the capacitance without any faradaic reaction. That is 2-4x the capacitance per area of ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 at EOT 0.4 nm, so a 5 fF node needs AR ~20-30 instead of 75.
why: Attacks fact 1 (charge wall) and fact 4 (fewer and shallower HAR etches); risk is double-layer charging time (<10 ns needed at nm scale) and self-discharge.

title: Ion-held charge: solid-electrolyte double-layer cell capacitor
idea: Swap the dielectric's role from a polarizing lattice to mobile ions: a 3-5 nm proton- or Li-conducting solid electrolyte between blocking electrodes piles ions into a ~0.5 nm Helmholtz layer at each plate, giving ~10-20 uF/cm2; ions travel <1 nm, so charging is ns-scale.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): effective k/t ~30x a ZrO2 stack, so a 10:1 cup reaches 5 fF and the 60-75:1 etch disappears; risks are electronic leakage and ion back-relaxation.

title: Cell-membrane double layer: solid ionogel replaces the MIM dielectric
idea: Cell membranes work inside electrolyte double layers. Replace the ZrO2 stack with a 5-10 nm crosslinked ionic-liquid gel so charge sits in two Helmholtz layers at ~20-40 uF/cm2, 3-5x a high-k MIM. At ~10 mS/cm ionic conductivity across a 10 nm gap, the ionic RC time is ~ns, fast enough for DRAM writes.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): 3-5x Cs per area lets AR fall from 70 to ~15-20, and self-discharge over hours is far longer than 64 ms. The risks are thermal budget and faradaic side reactions.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer capacitor replaces dielectric polarization
idea: Invert 'capacitance comes from electronic dielectric polarization' -> use an ionic double layer. A 3-5 nm solid proton or Li-ion electrolyte between electrodes forms an electric double layer of ~10-20 uF/cm^2, versus ~2.6 uF/cm^2 effective in today's pillar stacks, so 5 fF needs only an AR ~10-15 cup.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) by 4-8x per area, removing the hardest HAR etch steps; risk is whether nanometer EDLs charge in nanoseconds and survive unlimited cycling.

title: Po: the capacitor is a puddle — solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor
idea: Po: the capacitor is a puddle. Extracted: replace the high-k pillar dielectric with a 2-3 nm solid polymer/ionogel electrolyte between blocking TiN electrodes; its electric double layer (~10-20 uF/cm2, 3-6x the effective areal capacitance of a 70:1 ZrO2 pillar) holds the bit charge non-Faradaically, so endurance stays electrostatic.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): the same ~5 fF from an aspect ratio ~15:1 instead of 60-75:1, removing the deepest etch and its mask cost. Ion relaxation speed in nm-thin films is the main risk.

title: Nanopore electric double-layer capacitor with 100x areal capacitance
idea: Worsen: depend on solid dielectrics capped near k 40. Flip: fill shallow nanopores with an ionic-liquid or solid-electrolyte layer so the storage node is an electric double-layer capacitor (~10-20 uF/cm2, ~100x a 5 nm high-k film), with nm diffusion distances keeping charging near nanoseconds.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall without high AR (fact 1): planar 5 fF at <20 nm pitch.

title: Printed ionogel double-layer capacitor shrinking the charge wall
idea: IFR: a dielectric one molecule thick. Closest achievable: print an ion gel (ionic liquid in polymer) between blocking electrodes; the electric double layer acts as a ~1 nm dielectric giving ~10 uF/cm^2 (hundreds of times a 5 nm high-k film), with nano-thin gels pushing charging toward sub-us.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF fits a planar ~0.05 um^2 pad with no high-AR etch; R2R printable.

title: Solid-ionic double-layer nanocapacitor replaces the high-k pillar
idea: Scarcity rule: no high-k dielectric allowed. Store the bit in an electric double layer: a 3-5 nm solid ionic conductor (LiPON or a proton-conducting oxide) between ion-blocking electrodes gives Helmholtz capacitance of ~10-20 uF/cm2, about 10x a ZrO2 stack, so a planar or <=5:1 cup reaches 5 fF. Sub-redox voltages keep it purely capacitive (no faradaic reaction), so each write only displaces ions by a few angstroms.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 10x areal capacitance turns a 70:1 pillar into a 5:1 cup, deleting the hardest etch and dielectric ALD steps; requires ion response under 10 ns at nm length scales.

title: Ca: mayenite electride cages trap electrons as lattice-site anions
idea: Use a thin crystalline C12A7 (Ca12Al14O33) film, whose sub-nanometre cages host electrons as anions, as the storage layer of a gate stack; a gate pulse loads or empties cages near the interface and the caged electrons shift the read transistor's threshold.
why: Electrons sit in designed, identical lattice cages rather than random defects, aiming at trap-like retention without the oxide wear that limits flash endurance; all abundant Ca/Al/O; cage stability under cycling is speculative.

title: Shallow-trap nitride liner turns the access transistor into the cell
idea: Scarcity rule: one transistor, no capacitor, no new material. Engineer the gate-stack SiN liner with shallow 0.6-0.8 eV traps that a 1.5 V pulse loads in ns by direct tunneling through 1.5 nm SiO2, shifting threshold for seconds; the shallow depth allows low-field cycling that avoids NAND-style oxide wear.
why: A ~4F2 1T cell from standard materials removes the capacitor (facts 1, 2) and its EUV layers (fact 4) while seconds of retention cut refresh; 1e15-cycle endurance is the risk.

title: Polarity-encoded piezo resonators read by RF echo, never switched
idea: Effect walk: sign of the piezoelectric coefficient. Nanoscale ferroelectric AlScN contour-mode resonators store the bit as the sign of d33; a tiny RF ping on a shared line excites 64 resonators at distinct frequencies, and each response phase (0 vs 180 degrees) reveals its polarization while most stored mechanical energy returns to the line.
why: Read is resonant and reversible (Q~1000 recovers energy), non-destructive (fact 8), and reads 64 bits per ping by frequency multiplexing, giving >10x lower read energy per bit than DRAM sensing; resonator area limits density.

title: Racetrack rows: ACT shifts a domain-wall track, tRCD hides it
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): keep DDR's ACT-then-READ page model. Map each row address to a shift position of perpendicular domain-wall racetracks under a line of read/write heads; ACT drives a current pulse that moves the tracks to that position within tRCD (~14 ns at ~500 m/s covers ~64 bits at 100 nm spacing), the heads latch the row into sense amps, and PRE writes it back.
why: One head per 64 bits instead of a transistor per bit gives ~10x cell-area density (facts 4, 7), magnetic storage needs no refresh and has no wear; domain-wall pinning variability sets the risk.

title: Bubble-memory precedent: federal rugged-memory purchase guarantee for domestic production
idea: Magnetic bubble memory survived years longer because U.S. military and aerospace buyers needed rugged storage. Replicate that with a DoD/DOE/automotive consortium that guarantees purchase of at least 10M units per year of a 125 C/10 y-qualified, U.S.-fabbed DRAM-class element for five years, paid only after qualification.
why: Demand certainty lowers capital risk for the first U.S. line, lifting U.S. manufacturability above today's ~1-2% share.

title: Cavendish NEMS fixed: contactless bistable buckled nanobeams
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory died from contact stiction and wear. Use a compressively pre-stressed SiN or TiN nanobeam (~1 um x 20 nm) that Euler-buckles up or down: side electrodes snap it between the two stable shapes without it touching anything, and a capacitive or piezoresistive pickoff reads which way it bows.
why: No contact means no stiction or wear (endurance 1e15+ plausible); nonvolatile mechanical state with zero leakage or refresh; GHz-class nanobeams switch in ~ns.

title: C: ten-fullerene cluster charge bit sensed through a silicon nanowire
idea: Self-assemble ~10 C60 molecules per cell on a thin tunnel oxide over a silicon nanowire; each fullerene accepts one electron at a sharp LUMO level and the bit is the collective threshold shift; with only ~10 electrons per bit, shot noise and molecular dropouts give ~1% errors that the code absorbs.
why: The storage node shrinks to ~5 nm with molecule-defined, identical charge levels, far below a 6F² capacitor (facts 1, 4); carbon comes from soot-derived fullerenes.

title: Mercury thermometer and electrowetting display: liquid-metal nanomeniscus bit
idea: Seal a gallium-alloy nanodroplet in a 20-nm SiO2 nanochannel with two pockets; electrocapillary actuation (as in electrowetting displays) pushes the meniscus into one pocket, where it bridges or opens a gap between two electrodes, and surface-tension pinning at a constriction holds it with zero power. Read is a resistance check; the liquid reforms perfectly every cycle.
why: Facts 3 and 9: nonvolatile, refresh-free and immune to row-hammer charge coupling; a liquid has no wear mechanism, so endurance could exceed 1e15; Ga oxidation and wetting control at 20 nm are the risks.

title: Tunnel-FET gain cell with steep-slope read amplification
idea: Combine a band-to-band tunneling FET (sub-30 mV/decade) as the read device with a small storage node in a 2T gain cell, so every 10 mV of stored voltage moves read current by about an order of magnitude. Storage nodes can be 0.5 fF or less at a 0.4 V swing, and reading never disturbs the node.
why: Facts 1, 8, 10: ~10x smaller Cs, 0.4 V operation for ~6x lower CV2 energy, and non-destructive read.

title: Po: a capacitor with negative size — negative-capacitance boosted storage stack
idea: Po: the capacitor has a negative size. Extracted: put a thin ferroelectric in series with the paraelectric storage dielectric, tuned so its negative-capacitance branch is stabilised; the stack's capacitance then exceeds the paraelectric alone (1/C = 1/C_DE - 1/|C_FE|), giving effective k of 70+ from k~40 films.
why: Delivers the 'k ~ 70' exit from the capacitor wall (fact 1) without AR 115. Hysteresis-free stabilisation is the risk.

title: Electrowetting nanodroplet that sits in one of two wells
idea: Worsen: hold bits with charge that escapes through any defect. Flip: seal a ~50 nm droplet of ionic liquid in a dumbbell cavity; an electrowetting pulse moves it to the left or right well, capillary pinning holds it there, and its position reads out as a capacitance difference.
why: Non-volatile and immune to leakage (fact 3), no high-k dielectric needed (fact 1); a fluid has no fatigue.

title: Snap-through nanodome bit copied from thermostat snap disks
idea: Fabricate a prestressed 20 nm SiN/TiN dome over each cell that, like a bimetal snap disc or keyboard tactile dome, has two stable buckled states; an electrode pulse snaps it up or down in ns and the gap change is read capacitively.
why: Facts 3 and 8: retention is mechanical, so no leakage and no refresh, and the capacitive read is non-destructive, removing restore energy.

title: Acoustic recirculating delay-line memory: bits stored as phonons in flight
idea: IFR: memory with no cells at all. Closest achievable: store bit streams as GHz acoustic pulses circulating in thin-film LiNbO3 or AlN on-chip delay loops (sound is 10^5x slower than light, so 1 mm holds ~1000 bits at 4 GHz), regenerated each lap by a small amplifier; many short loops keep average latency near 100 ns.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): needs no capacitors and no fine lithography, only piezo films; fits streaming KV-cache and weight traffic that is accessed sequentially.

title: Ferroelastic twin-domain bit read by piezoresistance
idea: Worsen: rely on polarization that fatigues as charged defects pile up. Flip: store the bit as the orientation of a ferroelastic twin domain (a strain state) in a nanopillar of a non-polar ferroelastic oxide, switched by a short strain pulse from an attached piezo film and read by orientation-dependent resistance.
why: Non-volatile with no free charge to leak (fact 3); potentially fatigue-free because no polar charge accumulates.

title: Ferroelectric tunnel door sealing a capacitor's charge
idea: Combine a ferroelectric tunnel junction with a storage capacitor: the only path into the node is a 2-3 nm ferroelectric barrier whose polarization toggles it between transparent and opaque (tunneling ratio >1e5). The door is switched open for a write and closed to lock the charge, while a separate gain transistor reads the node without opening it.
why: Zero refresh while keeping charge storage (unlimited reads); the ferroelectric switches only on writes; closed-state tunneling must reach sub-aA levels.

title: Veneer-stacked hBN: sliding ferroelectric bit from boron and nitrogen
idea: Like plywood veneers laid at controlled grain angles, stack two hBN monolayers in parallel (AB/BA) alignment so out-of-plane polarization flips with a one-third-lattice interlayer slide. A graphene channel underneath reads it non-destructively as a resistance shift.
why: Facts 8 and 10: non-destructive read and near-fatigue-free sliding switching at <1 V, from B, N and C only. Being atomically thin, it fits monolithic 3D tiers.

title: Po: one cell holds a byte — big analog cells on glass
idea: Po: a single cell holds a whole byte. Extracted: invert scaling: make cells ~400x larger at 250 nm nanoimprint rules on glass panels (area cost ~1/5,000 of silicon) so each ~10 fF node has kT/C noise ~0.6 mV and 256 charge levels (8 bits) fit in 1 V, read with time-to-digital ramp sensing and re-quantised on every refresh.
why: 8 bits/cell x ~5,000x cheaper area / ~400x larger cell is roughly 100x lower $/GB. Trade-offs: slow multi-step sensing and leakage drift handled by frequent re-quantising refresh.

title: Circulating CCD loop memory with refresh built into the motion
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: store bits as charge packets marching around short (64-256 stage) buried-channel CCD loops at ~2F gate pitch with no per-bit transistor; one floating-gate amplifier per loop regenerates each packet as it passes, so refresh is inherent and there is no capacitor or access device.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 7: ~2-3F2 per bit with no capacitor; GHz loop rotation gives tens of ns average latency, best for streaming AI weights.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate capacitor with k near ten thousand
idea: Cryogenic quantum-computer controllers can use SrTiO3, whose permittivity climbs to ~1e4 near 4 K because quantum fluctuations suppress ferroelectric order, giving tens of fF in a planar 0.01 um2 cell. The generalizable version strain-tunes SrTiO3/KTaO3 superlattices on scandate-like buffers so the incipient-ferroelectric permittivity peak sits at 300-350 K, targeting k~300-1000.
why: Beats the k~70 requirement of fact 1 by 5-100x so the 60-75:1 pillar collapses to a planar stack; dead-layer and leakage control in sub-10 nm films is the hard part.

title: Gen-10.5 display glass memory trades density for cheap area
idea: Invert 'cost per bit comes from shrinking the cell' -> buy area instead. A Gen-10.5 glass sheet is ~9.6 m^2 (~140 300-mm wafers); build 1T1C cells at ~1 um^2 with planar 20 fF MIM capacitors and IGZO access (retention minutes, refresh nearly gone), giving ~1 TB of cells per sheet in under-utilized display fabs.
why: At ~$100/m^2 backplane cost that is under ~$1/GB of raw cells with no EUV or HAR etch (facts 1, 4) and no new $15B fab; micron lines limit speed and energy, so it serves as a CXL capacity tier.

title: One heavy-metal strip: forward to write, backward to read
idea: Rearrange the spintronic stack around one effect run both ways: a perpendicular nanomagnet on a Pt or Bi2Se3 strip is written by spin-orbit torque (charge to spin) and read by the inverse, a GHz pulse excites precession whose spin pumping yields an inverse-spin-Hall voltage whose sign is the bit; no MgO tunnel barrier.
why: Endurance and refresh (fact 3): nonvolatile with no barrier to break down, aiming at DRAM-like unlimited cycles; drops the tungsten-heavy MTJ stack; risk is a uV-scale read signal.

title: Balloon on sweater: contact-electrified charge tapped onto a pad
idea: Stimulus 'balloon rubbed on a sweater' -> a biased nanocantilever taps a trap-rich dielectric pad (e.g., Si3N4) to deposit or strip a few hundred electrons by contact electrification; the trapped charge gates a sense FET below. No tunnel current crosses an oxide, so there is none of Flash's oxide wear.
why: Nonvolatile charge storage with years of retention and no refresh (fact 3), yet endurance is not limited by tunnel-oxide damage; no storage capacitor (fact 1).

title: Electromechanical parametron: bit stored as oscillation phase
idea: Worsen: store bits as static levels that drift and leak. Flip: store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped high-Q NEMS resonator (Goto's parametron revived mechanically); the shared pump line continuously sustains whichever phase was seeded, so the state cannot leak away.
why: Replaces refresh with continuous low-power pumping (fact 3), needs no capacitor (fact 1), and phase coding is noise-robust so voltages can drop (fact 10).

title: Prion-templated martensite variants: compatible-lattice ferroelastic flip for endless cycling
idea: Prions convert their neighbours by templating their fold. Use a shape-memory-alloy film (TiNiCu-type) tuned so its martensite twin variants meet at geometrically compatible interfaces, the condition that let such films survive 10^7+ transformation cycles. A piezoelectric strain pulse switches a 20 nm cell between two variants, a remaining seed of the target variant templates fast growth, and the variants' anisotropic resistivity reads the bit.
why: Non-volatile, diffusionless switching (ns, low energy, with no melt as in PCM), with endurance limited only by lattice compatibility. No chalcogenides and no EUV.

title: B: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN stores bits in stacking order
idea: Use parallel-stacked bilayer hexagonal BN, whose interlayer polarization flips when one layer slides by a third of a bond length (AB to BA), as a gate dielectric; the stacking state shifts the channel threshold and is read non-destructively.
why: Sliding switching moves no ions, so fatigue should be very low; no capacitor; B and N are abundant with U.S. borate supply; aligned wafer-scale bilayer growth is the risk.

title: Transistor-less alien: tunnel-diode Goto-pair latch with picoamp standby
idea: An alien that never invented the transistor builds memory from negative resistance. Two series resonant tunneling diodes form a bistable 'Goto pair' latch whose standby current is set by the RTD valley current (~pA), giving an SRAM-like, refresh-free bit in about 4F².
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor (fact 1), in far less area than a 6T SRAM.

title: Eliminate tall pillars: Langmuir-Blodgett perovskite nanosheets give planar high-k capacitors
idea: Eliminate the 3D pillar: transfer 3-5 monolayers of exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr2Nb3O10 perovskite nanosheets from a water trough by Langmuir-Blodgett onto storage electrodes, giving a 5-10 nm dielectric with k~150-200 that stays high when thin because there is no dead layer; a 5 fF cell then needs only a short cup.
why: Meets the fact-1 k~70 target with ~2-3x the capacitance per area of ZAZ, cutting AR to ~25 (fact 4); room-temperature water processing uses no vacuum gases; risks are leakage at sheet edges and conformality.

title: Mongolian yurt: dry-peeled single-crystal BaTiO3 membranes, reusable substrate
idea: A herder carries a yurt in pieces and pitches it anywhere, dry. Grow single-crystal BaTiO3 on graphene-coated substrates by remote epitaxy, peel the membrane off mechanically with a dry stamp, and laminate it onto CMOS as the storage layer; the substrate is reused hundreds of times.
why: A single-crystal ferroelectric storage layer with low fatigue (facts 1, 3) without high-temperature steps on CMOS. There is no sacrificial wet etch or CMP, a more than 10x water cut.

title: Beekeeper's honeycomb: vapor-grown MOF crystal of dipolar molecular rotors
idea: A beekeeper fills a honeycomb one cell at a time. Convert an ALD ZnO film into a ZIF-type metal-organic framework by exposing it to linker vapor (no solvothermal bath), using linkers that carry dipolar rotors. A field aligns the rotors, a rotational energy barrier locks them, and the polar bit is read capacitively.
why: A molecular-scale, non-volatile dipole bit (facts 1, 3). The process is gas-phase and low-temperature with no solvent or UPW rinse, using more than 10x less water than a capacitor module.

title: Photochromic sunglasses: electrically switched diarylethene molecular bit
idea: Diarylethenes flip between open (insulating) and closed (conjugated, ~100x more conductive) isomers; anchor a monolayer in a 10-nm crossbar junction and switch it by field-assisted electrochemical ring closing/opening at ~1-2 V instead of light, reading conductance nondestructively, with thousands of molecules per bit for statistical robustness.
why: Density and capital: storage defined by a molecular monolayer at crossbar 4F2 with relaxed litho, thermally bistable and non-volatile; fatigue (~1e4-1e5 cycles today) must improve by ~1e10 to be DRAM-class.

title: Si: 100-tier deposited polysilicon floating-body cells, grain leakage tolerated
idea: Deposit alternating poly-Si/oxide layers as in 3D NAND and form capacitorless floating-body cells whose stored holes set the threshold; grain-boundary leakage makes ~1% of cells retain too briefly, which the code covers, so no single-crystal Si/SiGe epitaxy or wafer bonding is needed.
why: Opens 3D DRAM beyond the ~26-tier break-even (fact 2) on existing 3D NAND toolsets; the 1% tolerance is what makes cheap polysilicon acceptable.

title: Garden hose: conductive ferroelectric domain wall opened or kinked off
idea: Stimulus 'garden hose' (flow on, or kinked off) -> in a thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa, a write pulse creates or erases a charged head-to-head domain wall bridging two electrodes; the wall conducts ~1000x more than the bulk, so read is a small nondestructive current and the wall stays put without power.
why: Nondestructive read with no restore (fact 8), no refresh (fact 3), and current-mode read that suits vertical stacking (fact 2).

title: Po: memory that never stops moving — vertical CCD 3D strings
idea: Po: memory that never stops moving. Extracted: reuse a 200-tier 3D-NAND word-line stack but clock its tiers as a charge-coupled device, shifting charge packets up and down the vertical channel (no tunnelling, no oxide wear) and regenerating them at a sense amplifier at the string top on each pass.
why: Inherits NAND's ~$0.05/GB cost structure (100x+ below DRAM contract price) with unlimited endurance. Trade-offs: serial ~1 us access per 200-bit string, circulation limited by channel leakage.

title: Superionic nanolayer pseudocapacitor packs 30x charge per pillar
idea: IFR: a capacitor with infinite charge density that charges instantly. Closest achievable: line the pillar with a ~3 nm superionic conductor (alpha-AgI or Cu2Se class, ionic diffusivity ~1e-5 cm^2/s) between blocking electrodes so ions cross the film in ~25 ns, storing pseudocapacitive charge 10-30x that of a dielectric of equal area.
why: Fact 1: delivers the Cs that AR 115 or k 70 would, at AR ~10-20; fewer deep-etch steps lower capital (fact 4).

title: Mercury delay line reborn in RF SAW-filter fabs on lithium tantalate
idea: The UNIVAC mercury tank stored bits as acoustic pulses circulating between transducers. Existing RF front-end filter fabs (LiTaO3/LiNbO3, 0.25-0.5 um litho, billions of units per year, some in the U.S.) can make folded SAW delay loops with interdigital transducers, paired with a CMOS regenerator die.
why: No cell structure; ~4 km/s acoustic velocity gives 50,000x more delay per mm than light, so 2 GHz x 1 us loops hold 2 kb each as a refresh-free streaming tier that offloads sequential DRAM traffic; value is capex and supply chain, not density.

title: Al: self-ordered anodic alumina pores replace EUV for capacitor holes
idea: Deposit a thick Al film over the cell array and two-step anodize it so the oxide self-organizes into a hexagonal nanopore lattice (pitch ~25-40 nm set by anodizing voltage, AR >100), registered by shallow pre-indents from the bit-line grid; the pores become the capacitor holes and the Al2O3 is the mold.
why: Hits the AR~115 needed for more charge (fact 1) with a wet electrochemical bath instead of an EUV layer plus a deep dry etch (fact 4); aluminum is abundant and U.S.-sourced.

title: Chain-cell PZT FeRAM on a Texas line with domestic electrodes
idea: Box = {medium: PZT polarization | access: chain architecture, each FeCap in parallel with its transistor and cells linked in series (4F2-class) | sense: destructive charge read with in-chain restore | integration: 3D trench FeCaps | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: Dallas-style PZT module using Missouri lead, Oregon zirconium, and LaNiO3 conductive-oxide electrodes from California lanthanum and Michigan nickel}. Conductive-oxide electrodes suppress PZT fatigue toward 1e12-1e14 cycles, and a small SRAM cache absorbs hot writes.
why: U.S. manufacturability: scales a production-proven domestic ferroelectric line from niche to bulk memory; refresh-free, with no Ir or Ru.

title: Eliminate the solid storage medium: electrowetting nanodroplet position bits
idea: Eliminate solid-state storage: each cell is a sealed 30-nm pore holding a liquid-metal or ionic-liquid nanoplug that electrowetting moves between its top and bottom halves; capillary pinning holds it without power, and the plug position changes the cell capacitance 5-10x for readout.
why: Nonvolatile and refresh-free with no crystal-lattice wear-out (fact 3); viscous motion over ~10 nm might take 10-100 ns, which is the speculative part.

title: Eliminate linear-only dielectrics: built-in-biased antiferroelectric zirconia storage capacitor
idea: Eliminate the assumption that the capacitor dielectric must be linear: use antiferroelectric ZrO2 between asymmetric ALD electrodes (TiN from TiCl4/NH3 vs RuO2, all with N2 purge, not argon) whose work-function difference biases the film onto the steep part of its double loop, so field-induced polarization adds 2-3x charge inside a 0-1 V window without full domain reversal.
why: Effective k~70-100 meets the fact-1 target without AR 115, using an ALD-only, rare-gas-free stack; risks are endurance of partial AFE switching (>1e15 needed) and temperature drift.

title: Spin-crossover molecular film switched electrically between spin states
idea: Sublime a ~10 nm Fe(II) spin-crossover film (triazole or bispyrazolylborate family) at <=200 C. Cooperative lattice strain gives a ~20 K-wide room-temperature hysteresis between low-spin and high-spin; field or charge-injection pulses switch it, and a vertical junction reads the 10-100x conductance or dielectric contrast.
why: A molecular-scale bistability set by lattice elasticity, with no charge to leak (fact 3). Uses abundant iron and organics and is compatible with top tiers.

title: Dense MRAM's heat-and-crosstalk wall broken by antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Early dense-MRAM efforts lost thermal stability at small sizes and high temperature, and stray fields coupled neighbouring bits. Store the bit in the magnetic-octupole order of noncollinear antiferromagnetic Mn3Pt (TN ~475 K), read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction: exchange-enhanced anisotropy and zero net moment give Delta > 60 at 125 C in a 20 nm cell with no stray-field crosstalk.
why: Grade-1 retention at sub-20 nm pitch; ps-scale antiferromagnetic dynamics allow fast SOT writes; no inter-cell coupling raises density.

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings replace per-bit transistors and capacitors
idea: Box = {medium: charge packets in buried-channel potential wells | access: three-phase clocked ring gates, no per-bit FET | sense: floating-diffusion source follower at the string end | integration: vertical 32-bit CCD strings in deep holes | substrate: Si | fab: 3D-NAND-style hole etch + conformal gate stack}. Each vertical hole is a 32-stage CCD; a random access shifts the string past one amplifier in <30 ns, and every access recirculates and re-amplifies the packets, so refresh happens as a side effect of normal shifting.
why: Facts 2, 4, 7: ~2F2 per bit with no capacitor and no access transistor; density scales with string length rather than lithography, and one amplifier per 32 bits shrinks the periphery.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayers soaked into existing capacitor trenches
idea: Worsen: develop a deposition tool for a new dielectric. Flip: use wet chemistry to self-assemble redox-active porphyrin monolayers inside existing MIM or trench test capacitors so each molecule stores discrete electrons at fixed redox potentials; the budget is chemistry, a probe station and 24 months of cycling tests.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~2-5x charge per area, and discrete redox states could give 2 bits per cell; capital-free validation.

title: Eliminate capacitor and access transistor: vertical 3D CCD charge-packet memory
idea: Eliminate both the per-bit capacitor and the per-bit access transistor: store bits as charge packets in the potential wells of a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel wrapped by 64-128 stacked gate tiers (3D-NAND-style), and clock them like a CCD to one sense node at the top of each string. A 4-phase clock at 2-4 GHz moves a packet one tier per phase, so a 64-tier string gives ~10-30 ns average access plus burst streaming.
why: Attacks fact 2 (no manufacturable 3D cell) and fact 4 by reusing the mature 3D-NAND channel-hole process with no capacitor and one transistor per string; potential 5-10x bits/mm2 at 64+ tiers; retention set by well dark current, refresh happens naturally as packets recirculate.

title: OFDM-style time-constant coding of eight nodes behind one transistor
idea: Borrow multicarrier telecom decoding: connect eight storage nodes to one access transistor through tunnel barriers of graded thickness (tau = 1, 2, 4 ... 128 ns); a read records the discharge transient and a matrix-pencil decoder recovers each node's charge.
why: 10x at same cost: 8 nodes share one transistor and contact, barriers are deposition-defined, so ~6x from sharing x 2 tiers with no extra masks.

title: Scheduled reverse-polarity detox pulses push oxygen vacancies back
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #9 Prior anti-action: during idle windows the controller swaps plate bias so every capacitor in a mat sees a brief inverted field (~-1.2 V, ~1 us), driving field-drifted oxygen vacancies and trapped charge back toward their as-built distribution before they form leakage percolation paths.
why: Fact 3: reverses the dominant wear mode instead of over-provisioning margin; could allow ~20% thinner dielectric and higher Cs.

title: Electrocyte stack: parallel-store, series-read capacitor quartet
idea: Electric eels get high voltage by firing thousands of thin electrocytes in series. Each cell stores its bit on four small sub-capacitors charged in parallel, and at read three in-cell switches restack them in series so the bitline sees about 4x the voltage. Each sub-capacitor needs only ~1.3 fF at AR ~20, instead of one 5 fF pillar at AR 70.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): trades voltage gain for charge, so the signal per fF is ~4x and the AR-70 etch goes away. The cost is extra in-cell devices, so it fits best in BEOL/3D tiers where area is cheap.

title: Bootstrapped T-switch gain cell zeroes leakage across its write path
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality + #25 Self-service: write the gain-cell storage node through two series transistors and drive their middle node from the cell's own source-follower output, the guard trick from electrometers and sample-and-hold circuits. The inner transistor then sees ~0 V drain-source, so subthreshold leakage collapses.
why: Fact 3: leakage down ~50-100x, stretching refresh from 64 ms to seconds with plain Si or oxide transistors.

title: Buried Ge quantum well holds holes behind a band-offset wall
idea: Effect walk: heterojunction band-offset confinement. A capacitorless cell stores holes in a 5-nm compressively strained Ge quantum well beneath a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset, not a leaky p-n junction, is the retention barrier, and stored holes shift channel threshold for a gain read.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and attacks the junction-generation leakage tail (fact 3), allowing a 4F2 vertical cell built with SiGe epitaxy already running in U.S. fabs.

title: Vinyl record pressing: nanoimprint-stamped storage-node arrays, no EUV
idea: Records are pressed from one nickel master: e-beam-write a single master of the storage-node hole array once, electroform nickel or Si daughter stamps, and replicate it on every wafer by UV nanoimprint followed by RIE and ALD fill; perfectly periodic cell arrays tolerate imprint defects far better than logic.
why: Fact 4 capital: replaces 1-3 EUV exposures (~$150M+ tool) for the storage-node layer with a ~$5M imprinter, cutting that layer's patterning capex 10-30x and easing a U.S. fab; a university e-beam writer plus imprinter can demonstrate 20-nm half-pitch arrays.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterns capacitor holes without EUV
idea: Scale shift from polymer molecules to wafer patterns: use high-chi block copolymers that self-assemble into hexagonal cylinders at 16-20 nm pitch, guided by a coarse ArF template, to define the storage-node hole array.
why: Capital intensity: removes 1-2 EUV layers per cell array; molecules define the pitch for free.

title: Wordline-as-heater in-field anneal rejuvenates aged capacitor dielectrics
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: drive controlled current through spare wordline/plate metal to heat one air-gap-isolated sub-array to ~300-400 C for milliseconds, annealing out trap and oxygen-vacancy build-up in the capacitor dielectric and access-transistor interface after its data are moved to a neighbor mat. The aged storage element heals in place instead of being scrapped.
why: Fact 3: reverses retention-tail drift; extends module life ~2-3x so the same wafer starts serve longer.

title: Core memory reborn as vortex-chirality nanorings threaded by crosspoint lines
idea: Shrink the 1950s ferrite core to a 40-nm CoFeB/NiFe nanoring whose bit is the clockwise/counter-clockwise flux-closure vortex, exactly the core's circumferential flux. Write by coincident half-currents in an X and a Y line threading the ring hole (the core's square-loop half-select), and read non-destructively through a small MTJ patch on one ring segment instead of the core's destructive sense wire.
why: Removes capacitor and access transistor (Facts 1, 3); flux closure has no stray field so rings pack at ~4F2 and stack in decks; zero refresh and ~zero standby; claims 2-3x density per area at equal F with 4 decks.

title: Leaky 3D NAND string with direct-tunneling nanodots for seconds retention
idea: Adapt 3D NAND but make it leak on purpose: replace the 5 nm tunnel oxide with 1.8 nm SiO2 plus Si nanodots so writes use direct tunneling in ~20 ns with no hot-carrier wear, retention is ~seconds, and the NOR-connected vertical array is refreshed like DRAM.
why: 10x at same cost: 100+ layers at 3D-NAND wafer cost exceed 10 Gb/mm2 vs ~0.5 for DRAM; direct tunneling avoids Fowler-Nordheim damage, targeting >1e12 cycles.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal to harden storage-node junctions
idea: Worsen: leave hydrogen-passivated interface traps that de-passivate and feed the leakage tail. Flip: replace the final forming-gas anneal with high-pressure deuterium, whose heavier isotope bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal de-passivation (the giant isotope effect), and test tail retention on purchased DRAM test wafers within 24 months.
why: Fact 3 leakage tail: if the worst 0.01% of cells improve 2-4x, refresh interval doubles, from a cheap drop-in process change.

title: Nanomechanical parametron storing the bit as oscillation phase
idea: Pump a ~1 um GHz nanomechanical or contour-mode AlN resonator at 2*f0 so it oscillates in one of two degenerate phases, 0 or pi. Write by briefly injecting a small f0 signal of the chosen phase, read by homodyne phase detection, and share one pump line across many frequency-multiplexed resonators.
why: The symmetry-broken phase ignores amplitude noise and has no charge-leakage tail (fact 3). Density is weaker, which suits radiation-hard or cryogenic niches.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch revived as refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Box = {medium: bistable node voltage between two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) | access: one Si FET | sense: standard bitline | integration: diodes stacked vertically on the drain | substrate: Si | fab: low-temperature epitaxy of delta-doped tunnel junctions}. The two NDR curves cross at two stable points held by valley current alone, so the cell is static like SRAM in a ~8F2 DRAM-like footprint.
why: Fact 3: no refresh and no capacitor, 3-4x denser than 6T SRAM; standby power is set by valley current, which must reach <1 pA per cell.

title: Water-released single-crystal BST membranes stacked as capacitor tiers
idea: Invert 'high-k must be deposited polycrystalline in place' -> grow perfect crystal elsewhere and transfer it. Epitaxial (Ba,Sr)TiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer is released as a freestanding membrane (k ~300-1000 vs ~40 for ALD ZrO2), laminated onto glass or foil carriers under oxide-TFT access, and the growth substrate is reused.
why: Beats fact 1's k~70 target with margin so capacitors go planar or AR<10; consumes no silicon wafer and reuses the growth wafer >50x (capital, quartz-crucible chokepoint); thin-film dead layers and transfer yield are the risks.

title: Capacitive-read crosspoint: hysteretic MFS stack, no access transistor
idea: Scarcity rule: no transistor at the cell. Each crosspoint is a metal/ferroelectric/semiconductor stack whose polarization leaves the semiconductor in accumulation or depletion, and a sub-coercive AC read pulse senses the 3-5x small-signal capacitance difference, drawing no DC sneak current and never disturbing the state. Only writes switch polarization.
why: Stackable 4F2 crosspoint without selectors (facts 2, 4, 7) with nondestructive read removing restore (fact 8); ferroelectric write endurance (~1e11) needs write-sparing.

title: Ferroelectric/paraelectric superlattice in stabilized negative capacitance, effective k ~80
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: stack ~1-nm HZO ferroelectric layers between Al2O3/ZrO2 paraelectric layers sized so the ferroelectric sits on its stabilized negative-capacitance branch, making the series stack capacitance larger than either layer alone, with no hysteresis. Contradiction resolved: thick (low-leakage) dielectric vs. high capacitance.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: reaching k_eff 60-90 at ~6 nm physical thickness cuts tunneling-leakage tail ~10x versus equal-EOT ZrO2.

title: Rack-scale erasure codes let cells skip most refreshes
idea: Jump from the cell to the rack: extend refresh to 1 s and accept that weak-tail cells flip, because data is striped with LDPC/erasure codes across 64 DRAM chips on several DIMMs; a rack scrubber repairs flips well before they accumulate.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth: ~15x fewer refreshes recovers 10-20% bandwidth and most idle refresh power.
